newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner funds move aims for global status.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner funds move aims for global status.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG, Germany's second largest commercial bank, said Friday it plans to merge its foreign institutional funds business under one roof, led by its newly-acquired U.S. unit, RCM Capital Management.

The bank, pushing its aim to become a global player in asset management, said the new unit, whose name and launch date have not been finalised, will have 900 staff worldwide and assets under management of more than $50 billion.

Led by RCM Capital Management, the division will bring in the institutional funds business of London's Kleinwort Benson International Management and the smaller Thornton & Co., which is active in Asia.
It was not yet clear if the division would be headquartered in San Francisco, where RCM is based.
Analysts welcomed the move, saying it made sense to give a management role to RCM, which is viewed as having the highest level of funds expertise in the Dresdner group.
